description: We're five Seattle innovators combining code, data, and design to help people find what moves in the infrared sky. For Planet X and SPHEREx, we built WANDERERS, a tool that shows real NASA SPHEREx, WISE and Gaia images and the evidence for what each moving object is. Our team is full, and we're using this page so all members can join officially.
summary:
In 1930, Pluto was found by flipping between two photos of the sky and spotting the one dot that moved. Today NASA has millions of sky photos, but no one can flip through them by eye, and clouds and city lights hide the sky from most people.

WANDERERS is a time machine for the night sky. It lines up sixteen years of real NASA infrared images of the same patch of sky (WISE in 2010, NEOWISE through 2024, SPHEREx in 2025 and 2026) and plays them as a flipbook, so anyone can watch a nearby star move. SPHEREx's 102 colours of light add each object's chemical fingerprint.

Every result comes with an evidence card: what we measured, what ESA's Gaia catalogue says, which checks passed and which failed, and what the view cannot show. Anything we cannot match to a known object is called a candidate, never a discovery.

A Sky Compass lets you point your phone at the sky and see the real sky above you, in any weather.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
WANDERERS lets anyone watch the sky move and see the evidence for what each object is.

  • Observatory: plays real WISE, NEOWISE and SPHEREx images of the same patch of sky from 2010 to 2026 as a flipbook. Circles show where every known Gaia star should be in each frame, so anything moving without one stands out. The target's position is measured in every frame and compared with the catalogue.
  • Infrared fingerprint: aperture photometry in every SPHEREx image builds a 0.75-5 micron spectrum with water, methane and CO/CO2 bands marked.
  • Evidence card: stated, readable rules turn the measurements into a classification and a confidence, and list every check that passed and failed. Unmatched objects are "candidates, never discoveries".
  • Sky Survey: an automated search of 28.3 billion NEOWISE detections across 14% of the sky found 23,299 moving stars, ranks them for people to check, and checks them against SPHEREx's newest images.
  • Sky Compass: point a phone at the sky to see real survey photos of what is above you, with stars and planets labelled, even indoors or under cloud.
  • Star database: about 12,000 stars, each with its path from 1900 to 2100 and across 50,000 years, learned from up to 13 historical catalogues.
  • Adaptive Explorer: Kids, Student, General and Research modes, so a 10-year-old and a researcher can each use it their own way.
  • Stays current: a weekly GitHub Action checks NASA IRSA for new SPHEREx releases and refreshes the data.

HOW IT WORKS
A Python pipeline downloads public images from NASA IRSA and MAST and catalogues from ESA's Gaia archive, measures each object in every frame, and writes plain data files. A static website plays them back, so it is free to host and needs no server. Methods follow NASA IRSA's SPHEREx tutorials.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
Students, teachers, stargazing clubs and anyone under a light-polluted sky can explore real NASA data with no install and no account, and learn to ask "how do we know?" The next Pluto may already be in these photos; WANDERERS puts the search method in anyone's hands.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE
It brings back the Pluto "blink" method for the infrared sky, and pairs it with an honesty rule built into the product: every number shows its source, and nothing is ever called a discovery.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
Honesty about limits (a "What this view cannot show" box on every card), privacy (Sky Compass computes on the phone and sends location only rounded to about 50 km; no accounts), accessibility (Day and Night themes, readable contrast, plain language), and testing (about 650 JavaScript and 1,200 Python tests run on every change).

TOOLS
JavaScript (HTML canvas), Node.js, Python (astropy, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, pyvo/astroquery, pyarrow), React and Vite, FastAPI, Aladin Lite, three.js, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare, and Claude Code as an AI coding assistant.

Source code (open source, MIT): https://github.com/kneha07/WANDERERS
